subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw approve workspace-wide CRUD and/or host system filesystem browsing in Mission Control, and what operator permission boundary should replace or sit beside the bootstrap-file allowlist?
rationale: The remaining request changes which files trusted operator clients can read or mutate, and current main deliberately separates read-only workspace browsing from allowlisted bootstrap-file edits.

options.title: Approve workspace-only path first
options.body: Use the current read-only `agents.workspace.*` contract as the base, review or replace the canonical workspace-management PR for scoped workspace CRUD, and defer host system filesystem access.

options.title: Keep bootstrap edits only
options.body: Leave Mission Control editing restricted to bootstrap files and treat arbitrary workspace or host browsing as out of scope for now.

options.title: Design host system scope separately
options.body: Open a separate security design for host filesystem browsing with explicit opt-in, read/write limits, auditing, and recovery UX before any implementation.

recommendation.title: Approve workspace-only path first
recommendation.body: Use the current read-only `agents.workspace.*` contract as the base, review or replace the canonical workspace-management PR for scoped workspace CRUD, and defer host system filesystem access.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged commits and issue discussion show direct ownership of the read-only workspace boundary and mobile file-browser rollout.
